name: Tiroler Genussabend
beschreibung:
Tyrol's capital fuses historic mountain food culture with sophisticated urban dining. An evening of culinary indulgence in Innsbruck ranges from traditional folkloric Tyrolean Evenings featuring live music and classic hearty feasts, to historic taverns accredited by the Tyrolean Innkeepers Guild, and award-winning fine dining overlooking the city lights.

Formats & Venues

The city's best-known dinner-and-show institution is the Tyrolean Evening with the Gundolf Family at the Alpensaal Messe. For over five decades, the Gundolfs have combined authentic brass music, lively Schuhplattler dancing, and yodelling with a classic three-course menu (traditional roast pork with sauerkraut and potatoes, or vegetarian options, followed by apple strudel). Dinner & Show packages run approx. €66–€69 for adults (children 6–14 ~€20; show-only tickets ~€39), lasting about 2.5 to 3 hours.

In the historic Old Town, beloved culinary bastions include the sprawling Stiftskeller beneath ancient vaults, as well as the 600-year-old Goldener Adler and Weisses Rössl, serving certified regional staples such as dumpling trios, Tiroler Gröstl, and local grey cheese (mains ~€16–€30). Along the riverbank, the Markthalle Innsbruck buzzes with evening bistros and wine bars. For avant-garde dining, four-toque establishment Oniriq and the rooftop Lichtblick present multi-course regional tasting menus (from €120).

Season & Bookings: Most taverns and dinner shows operate year-round. Evening reservations are strongly recommended on weekends.

Getting There

Venues across central Innsbruck are comfortably accessed via the IVB tram and bus network. Tram Line 1 conveniently connects the Bergisel, Marktplatz (Old Town entrance / Markthalle), and Messe (Alpensaal) without changing lines. Public transit is free for holders of the Innsbruck Card or the regional Welcome Card.

Tips

  • Families: The Tyrolean Evening Gundolf is very family-friendly, offering lively performances and heavy discounts for children (under 6 free, ages 6–14 ~€20 with dinner). Traditional inns provide relaxed settings and kids' portions.
  • Dogs: Welcomed on leash in historic beer halls and inns; not recommended at music show venues due to volume.
  • Guided Food Tours: Guided food walks take guests behind the counters of local butchers, bakers, and cheesemongers.
